archetype.name: Gunslinger (vertical)
archetype.definition: A rhythm-and-shot passer who makes his living pushing the ball 10-plus yards downfield inside a run-first Harbaugh offense, accepting sacks and incompletions as the cost of chunk plays.

report.headline: A rebuilt McCarthy is hitting the deep ball; the short game hasn't followed.
report.take:
McCarthy arrives in New York as the third Giants starter of the year, after Jaxson Dart and Jameis Winston. His 2026 sample is tiny: a handful of snaps in Week 5, a relief appearance at 40% of snaps against New Orleans, then one full start, a win at Houston. That's 49 attempts, not enough to call anything settled. What it does show is a very different passer from the one who finished 2025 in Minnesota with a 57.6% completion rate, a -5.7 CPOE (56th of 63) and 12 interceptions in 10 games. This year his CPOE is +6.87 (6th of 47), his bad-throw rate is down 6.7 points, and he's getting the ball out faster, at 2.85 seconds against 3.02 last year.

The production is almost all vertical. On throws of 10-plus air yards he's at 1.224 EPA per play with a 19.1 CPOE and a two-thirds success rate. Deep balls alone have added 13.7 EPA, and the 10-19 yard window another 12. That's why his 10.1 yards per attempt ranks first among qualifiers. Malik Nabers is the main beneficiary at 0.572 EPA per target. Everything under 10 yards has gone the other way: -0.3 EPA per play, a 26% success rate, and his only interception came on a short throw. On third down he has converted 22.2% while facing an average of 9.3 yards to go. In the red zone he's completed one of five.

The box score hides two things. The first is volume. Harbaugh's offense passes 8.4 points less often than situations predict (30th of 32), so even good efficiency turns into modest raw numbers. He ranks 36th in passing yards per game and 40th in fantasy points per game while ranking 13th in EPA per dropback. The second is the touchdown rate. One TD on 49 attempts (2%, 42nd) is mostly red-zone noise on five snaps. It's more likely to rise than to define him; he threw 11 TDs in 10 games last year.

The question is how much of the downfield accuracy survives a bigger sample. A 22.3 deep CPOE on 10 attempts will come down. Still, the improvements in CPOE, bad-throw rate and time to throw all point the same way, which looks more like real development than a hot week. The sacks are the trait that carried over. His pressure-to-sack rate was poor in 2025 and is worse now on few pressures, and he took three sacks in his only start.

strengths.title: Accuracy and efficiency past 10 yards
strengths.body: His throws of 10-plus air yards produce 1.224 EPA per play with a 19.1 CPOE, and they account for almost all his value. They come from timing throws in the intermediate window and connected deep shots off a run-heavy script. The rate will come down from 21 attempts, but intermediate passing in particular is a repeatable skill.

strengths.title: Real jump in ball placement
strengths.body: Compared with 2025, his CPOE is up 12.6 points and his bad-throw rate is down 6.7, with a quicker release. Three metrics moving together is harder to dismiss as noise than one hot split. The 2025 version ranked near the bottom of the league in all of these.

strengths.title: Feeding Nabers effectively
strengths.body: Nabers has drawn 15 targets at 0.572 EPA each, and the offense works when McCarthy hunts that matchup downfield. Malachi Fields and Isaiah Likely have also been positive. It's a target tree he can lean on as long as Nabers stays the focus.

concerns.title: Short game and third downs failing
concerns.body: Throws under 10 yards are at -0.3 EPA with a 26% success rate, and third downs are converting 22.2% of the time. He's turning chunk gains into stalled drives when the defense takes the deep look away. Some of this is a tiny sample, but last year's struggles with efficiency suggest the underneath game isn't a given.

concerns.title: Pressure turns into sacks
concerns.body: He's rarely pressured, but half his pressures have become sacks, last among qualifiers, and he took three in his lone start. His 2025 pressure-to-sack rate also ranked poorly, so this looks like a trait rather than noise. It's partly the price of hunting downfield instead of checking down.

concerns.title: Low volume in a run-first offense
concerns.body: The Giants are 30th in pass rate over expected, which caps his attempts and his counting stats. That's a role constraint rather than a flaw, but it means efficiency won't turn into big fantasy lines. His red-zone work (1-for-5) hasn't yet made up for it.

trend.note: Both meaningful outings produced almost identical passing EPA (5 in relief, 5.6 in the start). His air yards dropped from the aggressive Week 6 relief role to a more measured Week 7, with a higher completion rate.

nextGame.headline: Worst pass rush in the league meets a sack-prone vertical passer
nextGame.body:
Philadelphia's defense is 29th in EPA and 24th against the pass, and it ranks last in both hit rate and sack rate. That's close to the ideal remedy for McCarthy's sack problem, giving him time to set up the intermediate and deep throws that carry his game. Opposing WR1s have outscored their averages by 3.9 points a game against Philly (28th), which sets up Nabers. The catch is volume. Philly is 31st against the run and plays as a mild run funnel, its offense is 30th in EPA, and the total is a low 40.5 with the Giants favored by 3.5. Harbaugh will likely lean on the ground game with a lead, so expect efficiency more than volume.

On the Eagles' side, linebacker Jihaad Campbell (82% of snaps) is out, which loosens the middle of the field, where McCarthy has been sharp on a small sample. Cornerbacks Jonathan Jones and Jakorian Bennett are out and Michael Carter II is questionable, thinning secondary depth rather than removing starters. For the Giants, Cam Skattebo is a game-time decision with Tyrone Tracy on IR. If Skattebo sits, Devin Singletary leads a thinner backfield and the run game may lose some of its punch, though probably not its share of the plays. Coming off a bye, McCarthy gets 14 days to prepare.

keyMatchups.title: Clean pockets versus his sack habit
keyMatchups.body: Philly ranks last in sack rate and hit rate, while McCarthy converts pressure into sacks more than any qualifier. If the rush stays this quiet, his biggest drive-killer is mostly off the table. Watch whether he still holds the ball when the first read is covered.

keyMatchups.title: Nabers against a leaky WR1 defense
keyMatchups.body: Opposing WR1s have outscored their averages against Philadelphia and posted 0.49 EPA per target (26th). That fits McCarthy's habit of feeding Nabers downfield. TE1s have been held under their averages, so Likely is the weaker lean.

keyMatchups.title: Run-heavy script caps his volume
keyMatchups.body: Philly is 31st in rush defense EPA, its offense is 30th, and the Giants already pass far below expectation. A lead plus an easy run game likely means another start in the high-20s for attempts. That caps his ceiling even if his efficiency holds.

nextGame.watch: Whether he can finish drives underneath and in the red zone, the part of his game that hasn't shown up yet, when Philly lets him sit in a clean pocket.

restOfSeason.body:
Expect an efficient, low-volume starter. The CPOE and bad-throw gains look real enough to keep him well above last year's version. The deep and intermediate rates will cool, with the 10-plus yard EPA likely drifting toward good rather than historic, and his yards per attempt settling in a range like 7.8 to 8.8. Touchdowns should pick up from a 2% rate that is mostly five red-zone snaps of bad luck. The sacks are likely to persist, since that has been his profile in both seasons.

The ceiling is set by Harbaugh's run-first approach: something like 26 to 31 attempts in a normal game, more only when trailing. His fantasy value will track game script and touchdown luck more than his talent. He is a better real-football quarterback right now than a fantasy one.
swingFactors: Whether the 10-plus yard accuracy holds over a larger sample
Giants' pass rate and game scripts under Harbaugh
Health of Nabers and the Skattebo-led backfield

confidence.note: 49 attempts and one start, though the gains over 2025 all point the same way.
